assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology to incretin-based therapy is a rare complete arc from peptide discovery to a therapeutic class that has transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care, with documented cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality and clarity are high, and the impact on clinical practice is very large and still growing.
assessment.attribution: Credit is crowded. Holst (physiology of GLP-1 and its insulinotropic action), Drucker (biology and clinical translation of GLP-1 and GLP-2) and Mojsov (peptide identification and synthesis) form a defensible triplet. Knudsen (liraglutide/semaglutide development) is a major contributor beyond three, and other early contributors such as Habener are not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple large outcome trials, regulatory approvals and years of real-world use independently confirm efficacy and safety. Timing is highly appropriate.
uncertainties: Allocation among basic discoverers versus drug developers is unresolved and the three-person limit excludes important contributors.
Whether the prize should honor the physiology or the pharmaceutical development is disputed in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells as a living therapy achieved durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, opening a new therapeutic modality in cancer. The concept (redirecting T cells with engineered receptors) is original and the clinical consequence is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CD28 costimulated chimeric receptor design) and June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T with 4-1BB) are central; Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials are foundational. Eshhar, Kuwana and others are not credited in this entry, so the configuration may be contested.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and over a decade of follow-up confirm durable responses in leukemia and lymphoma. Limits remain in solid tumors, toxicity and access, but the core discovery is established.
uncertainties: Priority claims for the first chimeric receptor concept are not fully represented in the supplied credit.
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancies, is still being characterized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstrating that TNF is a dominant driver in rheumatoid arthritis, and that its blockade controls disease, established cytokine-targeted therapy for chronic inflammatory disease and changed outcomes across rheumatology, gastroenterology and dermatology. The logic from mechanism to clinical proof is unusually clear.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly carried the mechanistic and clinical proof-of-concept work and are the natural pair; the supplied credit supports a clean two-person configuration. Contributions from antibody developers and trialists beyond them are real but secondary.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: decades of use, multiple agents and biosimilars, and consistent independent confirmation. Recognition would not be premature, and delay carries little risk of interpretive reversal.
uncertainties: Some may view the biologic drug development as separable from the discovery, but the supplied attribution is stable.
Many tumor-necrosis-factor biology contributors are outside this entry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided cell-type-specific, millisecond control of excitable cells and has become a foundational method in neuroscience, with expanding translational use including vision restoration. Originality and breadth of impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Credit is the main difficulty: six names are supplied. Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsin, Deisseroth established its neuronal use and broad application toolkit, while Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck have strong claims. Any three-person choice leaves out major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature as a tool with thousands of independent applications, though clinical benefit is still early.
uncertainties: Three-person limit conflicts with a plausibly larger set of decisive contributors.
Whether a methods advance fits the physiology-or-medicine framing relative to a disease-relevant discovery is a matter of judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of BCL-2 as a survival rather than proliferation factor, and its role in controlling apoptosis, defined a central mechanism of cancer cell resistance and led directly to BH3-mimetic therapy (venetoclax) in leukemia. The discovery is conceptually important and clinically validated.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams led the Bcl-2 family cloning and functional programme; Vaux demonstrated the cell-survival function with Cory in the 1988 work. Strasser is a key later contributor, and Korsmeyer and Tsujimoto are not on the list but were involved in the translocation and early gene characterization, so allocation is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Mature: apoptosis regulation has been confirmed extensively, and venetoclax approvals provide strong translational validation.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior prize-recognized apoptosis work (Brenner, Horvitz, Sulston) may temper novelty.
Credit for the original translocation and gene identification is shared across groups not fully represented.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explains how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immune responses, connecting infection, autoimmunity (including interferonopathies and lupus-like disease), and cancer immunity. It is a clear, widely generalized mechanism that has launched a large therapeutic effort.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide cGAMP second messenger, which is the decisive mechanistic step; Barber discovered STING. Ishikawa, Sun and Wu also made important contributions but a two-person configuration is defensible.
assessment.maturity: The mechanism is robustly confirmed, though clinical translation of STING agonists and inhibitors is not yet established. Recognition would rest on mechanistic impact rather than therapeutic proof.
uncertainties: Allocation between Barber (STING) and the cGAS team, and the roles of other contributors, may be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of BCL11A as a repressor of fetal hemoglobin, from human genetics through mechanism to gene-editing therapy, led to an approved cure-oriented treatment for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia. It is a clear and elegant genotype-to-therapy story.
assessment.attribution: Orkin and Sankaran defined BCL11A's role and mechanism, and Bauer contributed the enhancer-targeting editing strategy. Thein's genetic association work is important and not included here; the supplied credit therefore leaves an unresolved allocation.
assessment.maturity: Approval of the editing therapy supports the biology, but treatment follow-up is relatively short and access is limited. Recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Long-term durability and safety of the editing therapy are not yet known.
A compound discovery whose human-genetic and editing parts may need different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification and cloning of IL-6 (BSF-2) and its receptor, and the demonstration that blocking IL-6 signaling treats rheumatoid arthritis, Castleman disease and other inflammatory conditions. This defined a second major cytokine-targeted therapeutic axis and has shown utility in severe inflammation including cytokine release syndrome.
assessment.attribution: Kishimoto and Hirano led the molecular characterization of IL-6 and its receptor; Kishimoto also drove tocilizumab development. The pair is a clear and coherent attribution, though others contributed to early IL-6 identification.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with long clinical use and consistent confirmation across indications. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Priority for early IL-6 activities discovered by several laboratories may complicate credit.
Impact is somewhat narrower than the leading candidates.
